name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# Affine locality for native pushforward base change
    13	
    14	This file supplies two generic reductions used when proving that a canonical base-change mate is
    15	an isomorphism.
    16	
    17	* `Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_affine` upgrades isomorphisms on every affine open to an
    18	  isomorphism of sheaves of modules.  It uses the affine-open basis and stalks, and does not impose
    19	  quasi-coherence or finiteness hypotheses.
    20	* The two `of_fromTildeΓ` lemmas upgrade an isomorphism, or a bijection, on global sections of
    21	  `Spec R` once the source and target affine presentations `fromTildeΓ` are already known to be
    22	  isomorphisms.
    23	
    24	The latter hypothesis is deliberately explicit.  The pinned Mathlib does not provide the general
    25	affine equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on `Spec R` and `R`-modules, so these lemmas do
    26	not assert that quasi-coherence alone constructs the two affine presentations.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	set_option autoImplicit false
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	open Scheme Scheme.Modules
    38	
    39	-- The composite defining `e.hom` unfolds only below reducible transparency.
    40	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    41	/-- A morphism between two modules on `Spec R` with known affine presentations is an isomorphism
    42	as soon as its map on the corresponding global-sections modules is an isomorphism. -/
    43	theorem Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_moduleSpecGammaFunctor_map_of_fromTildeGamma
    44	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {M N : (Spec R).Modules}
    45	    [IsIso M.fromTildeΓ] [IsIso N.fromTildeΓ] (φ : M ⟶ N)
    46	    (h : IsIso ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R)).map φ)) : IsIso φ := by
    47	  have key : M.fromTildeΓ ≫ φ =
    48	      (tilde.functor R).map ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R)).map φ) ≫ N.fromTildeΓ :=
    49	    ((Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓNatTrans (R := R)).naturality φ).symm
    50	  let iM := asIso M.fromTildeΓ
    51	  let iN := asIso N.fromTildeΓ
    52	  let iG := @asIso _ _ _ _ ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R)).map φ) h
    53	  let e : M ≅ N := iM.symm ≪≫ (tilde.functor R).mapIso iG ≪≫ iN
    54	  have he : e.hom = φ :=
    55	    calc e.hom
    56	        = iM.inv ≫ ((tilde.functor R).map ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R)).map φ) ≫
    57	            N.fromTildeΓ) := rfl
    58	      _ = iM.inv ≫ (M.fromTildeΓ ≫ φ) := by rw [key]
    59	      _ = φ := Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc iM φ
    60	  rw [← he]
    61	  exact e.isIso_hom
    62	
    63	-- The functor map and `Hom.app` are definitionally equal only after unfolding a non-reducible
    64	-- functor field.
    65	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    66	/-- Global-section form of
    67	`Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_moduleSpecGammaFunctor_map_of_fromTildeGamma`. -/
    68	theorem Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_bijective_appTop_of_fromTildeGamma
    69	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {M N : (Spec R).Modules}
    70	    [IsIso M.fromTildeΓ] [IsIso N.fromTildeΓ] (φ : M ⟶ N)
    71	    (h : Function.Bijective (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app φ (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))) :
    72	    IsIso φ := by
    73	  refine Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_moduleSpecGammaFunctor_map_of_fromTildeGamma φ ?_
    74	  rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective]
    75	  have hfun : ⇑(ConcreteCategory.hom ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := R)).map φ)) =
    76	      ⇑(ConcreteCategory.hom (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app φ (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))) := rfl
    77	  rw [hfun]
    78	  exact h
    79	
    80	/-- A morphism of scheme modules is an isomorphism if its section map is an isomorphism on every
    81	affine open.  The proof computes stalks on the affine-open basis, then reflects the resulting
    82	isomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves. -/
    83	theorem Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_affine
    84	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N)
    85	    (h : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → IsIso (φ.app U)) :
    86	    IsIso φ := by
    87	  let f := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).map φ
    88	  have happ (U : X.Opens) (hU : U ∈ X.affineOpens) :
    89	      IsIso (f.hom.app (.op U)) := by
    90	    dsimp [f]
    91	    exact h U hU
    92	  have hstalk (x : X) :
    93	      IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map f.hom) := by
    94	    rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective]
    95	    constructor
    96	    · apply TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis X.isBasis_affineOpens
    97	      intro U hU
    98	      exact (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective (f.hom.app (.op U))).mp
    99	        (happ U hU) |>.1
   100	    · intro t
   101	      obtain ⟨U, hxU, hU, s, rfl⟩ :=
   102	        TopCat.Presheaf.exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis X.isBasis_affineOpens
   103	          (TopCat.Sheaf.presheaf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).obj N)) x t
   104	      letI : IsIso (f.hom.app (.op U)) := happ U hU
   105	      refine ⟨(TopCat.Sheaf.presheaf
   106	          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).obj M)).germ U x hxU
   107	        (inv (f.hom.app (.op U)) s), ?_⟩
   108	      rw [TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply]
   109	      simp
   110	  letI (x : X) := hstalk x
   111	  haveI : IsIso f := TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_of_stalkFunctor_map_iso f
   112	  haveI : IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) := by
   113	    change IsIso f.hom
   114	    infer_instance
   115	  exact isIso_of_reflects_iso φ (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X)
   116	
   117	/-- A morphism of scheme modules is an isomorphism if its restrictions to a family of opens
   118	covering every point are isomorphisms.  The proof transports the restricted stalk maps across
   119	`restrictStalkNatIso`, then reflects the resulting isomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves. -/
   120	theorem Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_restrict_cover
   121	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N)
   122	    {ι : Type*} (U : ι → X.Opens)
   123	    (hcov : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)
   124	    (hiso : ∀ i, IsIso ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ)) :
   125	    IsIso φ := by
   126	  let f := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).map φ
   127	  have hstalk (x : X) :
   128	      IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map f.hom) := by
   129	    change IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map ((toPresheaf X).map φ))
   130	    obtain ⟨i, hx⟩ := hcov x
   131	    let xU : (U i).toScheme := ⟨x, hx⟩
   132	    letI hres : IsIso ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ) := hiso i
   133	    haveI hpres : IsIso ((toPresheaf (U i).toScheme).map
   134	        ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ)) :=
   135	      Functor.map_isIso _ _
   136	    haveI hr : IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab xU).map
   137	        ((toPresheaf (U i).toScheme).map ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ))) :=
   138	      Functor.map_isIso _ _
   139	    let eM := (restrictStalkNatIso (U i).ι xU).app M
   140	    let eN := (restrictStalkNatIso (U i).ι xU).app N
   141	    letI heM : IsIso eM.hom := eM.isIso_hom
   142	    letI heN : IsIso eN.hom := eN.isIso_hom
   143	    have hnat :
   144	        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab xU).map
   145	              ((toPresheaf (U i).toScheme).map ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ)) ≫
   146	            eN.hom =
   147	          eM.hom ≫ (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map
   148	            ((toPresheaf X).map φ) := by
   149	      exact (restrictStalkNatIso (U i).ι xU).hom.naturality φ
   150	    haveI hcompLeft : IsIso (
   151	        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab xU).map
   152	              ((toPresheaf (U i).toScheme).map ((restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map φ)) ≫
   153	            eN.hom) :=
   154	      IsIso.comp_isIso
   155	    haveI hcompRight : IsIso (eM.hom ≫
   156	        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map ((toPresheaf X).map φ)) := by

     9	/-!
    10	# Pullback of unit and tilde modules
    11	
    12	This file supplies the unit and affine tensor dictionaries needed by native pushforward base
    13	change.  For every map of schemes, inverse image on opens is final: the top open gives a terminal
    14	object in each structured-arrow category.  Consequently, pullback carries the unit module
    15	canonically to the unit module.
    16	
    17	For a ring map `A \to B`, pullback along `Spec B \to Spec A` takes the tilde sheaf of an
    18	`A`-module to the tilde sheaf of its scalar extension to `B`.
    19	
    20	The proof uses uniqueness of left adjoints.  The only comparison required on the right-adjoint
    21	side is that global sections after pushforward along `Spec.map phi` are restriction of scalars
    22	along `phi`; on underlying sections this is restriction along `top <= (Spec.map phi) ^-1(top)`,
    23	which is the identity.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	open Scheme Scheme.Modules
    35	
    36	/-! ## Pullback of the unit module -/
    37	
    38	private noncomputable def opensMapStructuredArrowTerminal {X Y : TopCat.{u}}
    39	    (f : X ⟶ Y) (U : Opens X) :
    40	    IsTerminal (StructuredArrow.mk (Opens.leMapTop f U)) :=
    41	  IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom
    42	    (fun s => StructuredArrow.homMk (Opens.leTop s.right) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))
    43	    (fun _ _ => by
    44	      apply StructuredArrow.hom_ext
    45	      exact Subsingleton.elim _ _)
    46	
    47	@[reducible]
    48	private noncomputable def opensMapFinal {X Y : TopCat.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    49	    (Opens.map f).Final where
    50	  out U := isConnected_of_isTerminal _ (opensMapStructuredArrowTerminal f U)
    51	
    52	/-- Pullback along any morphism of schemes carries the unit module to the unit module by an
    53	isomorphism.  No openness, flatness, or finiteness hypothesis is needed. -/
    54	theorem Scheme.Modules.isIso_pullbackObjUnitToUnit {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    55	    IsIso (SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit f.toRingCatSheafHom) := by
    56	  letI : (Opens.map f.base).Final := opensMapFinal f.base
    57	  infer_instance
    58	
    59	/-- The canonical isomorphism from the pullback of the unit module to the unit module. -/
    60	noncomputable def Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    61	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) ≅
    62	      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf :=
    63	  @asIso _ _ _ _ _ (Scheme.Modules.isIso_pullbackObjUnitToUnit f)

    67	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in

    91	          (⊤ : (Spec B).Opens) ≤ Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)).op).hom x

    95	          (⊤ : (Spec B).Opens) ≤ Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤))

    97	        (congrArg (fun r => r • (N.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top :
    98	            (⊤ : (Spec B).Opens) ≤ Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)).op).hom x)
    99	          ((congrArg (fun (k : Γ(Spec B, Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤) ⟶ Γ(Spec B, ⊤)) =>
   100	              k.hom (((Spec.map phi).app ⊤).hom ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv.hom a)))
   101	            (ringRestrictionPreimageTopEqId (Spec.map phi) le_top)).trans
   102	           ((congrArg (fun (psi : A ⟶ Γ(Spec B, ⊤)) => psi.hom a)
   103	              (Scheme.ΓSpecIso_inv_naturality phi)).symm))) }

   106	private lemma pullbackTildeGammaBridgeHom_isIso {A B : CommRingCat.{u}}
   107	    (phi : A ⟶ B) (N : (Spec B).Modules) :
   108	    IsIso (pullbackTildeGammaBridgeHom phi N) := by

   111	    (⊤ : (Spec B).Opens) ≤ Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)).op).hom x)
   112	  rw [modulesRestrictionPreimageTopEqId (Spec.map phi) N le_top]
   113	  exact Function.bijective_id

   116	private noncomputable def pullbackTildeGammaBridge {A B : CommRingCat.{u}}
   117	    (phi : A ⟶ B) :
   118	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map phi) ⋙ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := A) ≅
   119	      moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := B) ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars phi.hom := by
   120	  refine NatIso.ofComponents
   121	    (fun N => @asIso _ _ _ _ _ (pullbackTildeGammaBridgeHom_isIso phi N))
   122	    (fun {N N'} h => ?_)
   123	  ext x
   124	  exact (congrArg (fun (k : Γ(N, Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤) ⟶ Γ(N', ⊤)) => k.hom x)
   125	    ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf h).naturality (homOfLE (le_top :
   126	      (⊤ : (Spec B).Opens) ≤ Spec.map phi ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)).op)).symm

   128	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   129	/-- Pullback along `Spec.map phi` carries a tilde module to the tilde of scalar extension.
   130	
   131	This is the affine `pullback of tilde = tilde of tensor product` comparison (Stacks 01HQ).
   132	It is canonical: it is the uniqueness isomorphism between two left adjoints of global sections
   133	with restriction of scalars. -/
   134	noncomputable def Scheme.Modules.pullbackTildeIso {A B : CommRingCat.{u}}
   135	    (phi : A ⟶ B) :
   136	    tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback (Spec.map phi) ≅
   137	      ModuleCat.extendScalars phi.hom ⋙ tilde.functor B :=
   138	  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq
   139	    (((tilde.adjunction (R := A)).comp
   140	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Spec.map phi))).ofNatIsoRight
   141	      (pullbackTildeGammaBridge phi))
   142	    ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj phi.hom).comp (tilde.adjunction (R := B)))

    12	This file transports that equivalence through `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.nativeModuleKSheafIso`,
    13	so the native `Scheme.Modules` object exposes the same comparison on its actual sections.
    14	The resulting map is an algebraic input to the canonical base-change mate; it does not assume
    15	that the mate itself is an isomorphism.

    45	    Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[B] Γ(D.nativeModule, ⊤) :=
    46	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
    47	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical pushforward base change for scheme modules
    10	
    11	For a cartesian square of schemes, `canonicalBaseChangeMap` is the Beck--Chevalley mate
    12	
    13	```text
    14	g^* f_* M --> f'_* (g')^* M.
    15	```
    16	
    17	The two coherence theorems identify its pullback followed by the counit with the pullback of
    18	the original counit.  Invertibility is deliberately not asserted here: it is a property of the
    19	module and square, not part of the construction of the canonical map.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	/-- The canonical Beck--Chevalley mate for pushforward along a cartesian square. -/
    31	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
    32	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    33	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    34	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    35	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback g ⟶
    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    41	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    42	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom)
    43	
    44	/-- Pulling back the canonical mate and evaluating recovers its defining pullback telescope. -/
    45	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit
    46	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    47	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    48	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    49	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    50	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    51	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M) =
    52	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    54	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom).app
    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    56	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    57	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    58	  rw [canonicalBaseChangeMap]
    59	  exact CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit _ _ _ M
    60	
    61	/-- After cancelling the pullback telescope, the base-changed counit is the pulled-back
    62	original counit. -/
    63	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel
    64	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    65	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    66	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    67	    ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    68	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    69	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).inv).app
    70	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    71	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    72	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    73	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M)) =
    74	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    75	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    76	  erw [canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit]
    77	  erw [Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc]
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	end AlgebraicGeometry

    35	The datum-level `sectionsMap` is already linear over the structure-sheaf map and
    36	commutes with restriction.  It therefore gives a morphism from the native module

    48	    { app := fun U ↦ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom <| AddMonoidHom.mk'
    49	        (fun s ↦ D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl s)
    50	        (fun s t ↦ D.sectionsMap_add B' le_rfl s t)
    51	      naturality := fun {U V} i ↦ by
    52	        ext s
    53	        change D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl
    54	            (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit i.unop.le s) =
    55	          gluedRes B' (D.baseChange B').pieces (D.baseChange B').unit

    57	            (D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl s)
    58	        exact (D.gluedRes_sectionsMap B' i.unop.le le_rfl le_rfl
    59	          (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (relCurveMap C B B') i.unop.le) s).symm }
    60	    (fun U r s ↦ by
    61	      change D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl
    62	          (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit le_rfl r s) =
    63	        gluedQsmul B' (D.baseChange B').pieces (D.baseChange B').unit le_rfl
    64	          (((relCurveMap C B B').app U.unop).hom r) (D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl s)
    65	      simpa only [Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app] using
    66	        D.sectionsMap_gluedQsmul B'
    67	          (W := U.unop) (W' := relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ U.unop)
    68	          (V := U.unop) (V' := relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ U.unop)

    70	
    71	@[simp]
    72	theorem nativeModuleSectionsMap_app_apply (U : (relCurve C B).Opens)
    73	    (s : Γ(D.nativeModule, U)) :
    74	    (D.nativeModuleSectionsMap B').app U s = D.sectionsMap B' le_rfl s :=
    75	  rfl
    76	
    77	/-- The native module rebuilt from the base-changed datum receives the geometric
    78	pullback of the original native module.  This is adjoint to `sectionsMap` on
    79	every open, with no flatness or finiteness hypothesis on `B → B'`. -/

    81	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C B B')).obj D.nativeModule ⟶
    82	      (D.baseChange B').nativeModule :=

    85	      (D.baseChange B').nativeModule).symm (D.nativeModuleSectionsMap B')

    92	      (relCurveMap C B B')).homEquiv D.nativeModule
    93	        (D.baseChange B').nativeModule (D.nativePullbackComparison B') =
    94	      D.nativeModuleSectionsMap B' := by
    95	  exact Equiv.apply_symm_apply _ _
    96	
    97	end
    98

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocusNative

     8	/-!
     9	# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract
    10	
    11	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
    12	This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
    13	always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
    14	`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
    15	arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
    16	explicit obligations.
    17	
    18	The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
    19	second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
    21	through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    42	
    43	/-! ## The native adapter contract -/
    44	
    45	/--
    46	A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
    47	cocycle datum.
    48	
    49	The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
    50	certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
    51	calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
    52	evaluation module.
    53	-/
    54	structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    55	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    57	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    58	  represents :
    59	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    60	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    61	  datum_class :
    62	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    63	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    64	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    65	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    66	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    67	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    68	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    69	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    70	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
    71	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    72	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    73	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    74	  h0_rank_one :
    75	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    76	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    77	
    78	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    79	
    80	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    81	
    82	/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.
    83	
    84	The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
    85	without weakening or adding hypotheses.
    86	-/
    87	noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    88	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    89	    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
    90	  { cover := P.cover
    91	    representative := P.representative
    92	    represents := P.represents
    93	    datum := P.datum
    94	    datum_class := P.datum_class
    95	    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    96	    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    97	    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    98	    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    99	    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
   100	    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
   101	    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
   102	    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }
   103	
   104	theorem nonempty_localPresentation
   105	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
   106	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
   107	  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩
   108	
   109	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   110	
   111	/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/
   112	
   113	/--
   114	An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
   115	consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
   116	`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
   117	choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
   118	-/
   119	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
   120	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   121	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   122	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   123	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
   124	        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
   125	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
   126	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   127	  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
   128	  intro A _ _ t
   129	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
   130	  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation
   131	
   132	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# Base change of the pinned cocycle datum (DAT-1, stage 1d-ii, the datum half)
    10	
    11	The `relCocycleBaseChange`-style base change of the basic-open cocycle datum
    12	(`informal/spec-dat-1.md` stage (1d-ii), first bullet; worksheet §3.2 — **this is the
    13	RE-5 transport interface**): along a `k`-algebra map `B → B'`, the generators, partition
    14	coefficients and transition units of a `Scheme.BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` push forward
    15	through the relative-curve comparison morphism `relCurveMap C B B'` to a datum over `B'`,
    16	with the pieces mapping to pieces (`Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`) and the partition/cocycle
    17	identities carried by `map_*`.
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appLE_resHom` — `appLE` commutes with restriction on
    20	  both sides (the workhorse; both sides collapse to one `appLE` by
    21	  `appLE_map`/`map_appLE` and proof irrelevance).
    22	* `relSectionsMap_basicOpen` — basic opens of compared sections are preimages of basic
    23	  opens.
    24	* `relCurveMap_appLE_overAlgebraMap` — the comparison intertwines the structure algebra
    25	  maps along `algebraMap B B'`, over **arbitrary** opens (the pullback-open case is the
    26	  landed `relSectionsMap_overAlgebraMap`).
    27	* `BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange` / `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange` — the datum base
    28	  change, with `pieces_baseChange` (pieces map to pieces).
    29	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionsMap` — the componentwise comparison of glued sections
    30	  `F_D(W) → F_{D'}(W')` for `W' ≤ relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ W`, additive
    31	  (`sectionsMap_add`), semilinear along `algebraMap B B'` (`sectionsMap_smul`),
    32	  commuting with restriction (`gluedRes_sectionsMap`), intertwining the piece
    33	  trivializations with the section comparison (`gluedTriv_sectionsMap`) and the
    34	  componentwise chart actions (`sectionsMap_gluedQsmul`) — the inputs of the stage
    35	  (1d-ii) term identifications and the RE-5 transport.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C B, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
    40	`(C ⊗ overSpec k B).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
    41	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    42	
    43	universe u
    44	
    45	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
    46	open Opposite
    47	
    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    49	
    50	/-! ## `appLE` against restriction, on arbitrary opens -/
    51	
    52	/-- **`appLE` commutes with restriction**: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, restricting the `appLE`
    53	image of a section equals the `appLE` image of the restricted section. Both sides are
    54	`f.appLE W PW'` of the section, by `appLE_map`/`map_appLE` and proof irrelevance of the
    55	inclusion witnesses. -/
    56	lemma Scheme.Hom.appLE_resHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X.Hom Y) {W' W : Y.Opens}
    57	    {PW' PW : X.Opens} (hW : W' ≤ W) (ePW : PW ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W) (ePW' : PW' ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W')
    58	    (hP : PW' ≤ PW) (s : Γ(Y, W)) :
    59	    X.resHom hP ((f.appLE W PW ePW).hom s) =
    60	      (f.appLE W' PW' ePW').hom (Y.resHom hW s) := by

    75	/-- **Basic opens base-change to basic opens**: the basic open of the compared section
    76	`relSectionsMap s` is the `relCurveMap`-preimage of the basic open of `s`. -/
    77	theorem relSectionsMap_basicOpen (V : C.left.Opens)
    78	    (s : Γ(relCurve C B, (fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)) :
    79	    (relCurve C B').basicOpen (relSectionsMap C B B' V s) =
    80	      relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((relCurve C B).basicOpen s) := by
    81	  have happ : relSectionsMap C B B' V s =
    82	      (relCurve C B').resHom
    83	        (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm :
    84	          (fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤
    85	            relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    86	        (((relCurveMap C B B').app ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom s) := by
    87	    have h := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
    88	      $(Scheme.Hom.appLE_map (relCurveMap C B B')
    89	        (le_refl (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)))
    90	        (homOfLE (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)).op)) s)
    91	    have h0 : ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    92	        (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)) le_rfl).hom s =
    93	        (((relCurveMap C B B').app ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom s) :=
    94	      congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
    95	        $(Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app (relCurveMap C B B')
    96	          (U := (fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))) s)
    97	    calc relSectionsMap C B B' V s
    98	        = ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    99	            ((fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
   100	            (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)).hom s := rfl
   101	      _ = (relCurve C B').resHom (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)
   102	            (((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
   103	              (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
   104	              le_rfl).hom s) := h.symm
   105	      _ = _ := by rw [h0]
   106	  rw [happ, Scheme.basicOpen_resHom,
   107	    ← Scheme.preimage_basicOpen (relCurveMap C B B') s,
   108	    ← relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V, ← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf]
   109	  congr 1
   110	  exact inf_eq_right.mpr ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le s)

   114	/-- `appLE` is invariant under an equality of morphisms. -/
   115	private lemma appLE_congr_hom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h : f = g) {U : Y.Opens}
   116	    {W : X.Opens} (e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
   117	    f.appLE U W e = g.appLE U W (h ▸ e) := by
   118	  subst h; rfl

   122	/-- **The comparison intertwines the structure actions, on arbitrary opens**: the
   123	`appLE` image of the structure pullback of `r : B` is the structure pullback of
   124	`algebraMap B B' r` (the landed `relSectionsMap_overAlgebraMap` is the pullback-open
   125	case `W = V_B`). -/
   126	theorem relCurveMap_appLE_overAlgebraMap {W : (relCurve C B).Opens}
   127	    {W' : (relCurve C B').Opens} (hle : W' ≤ relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ W) (r : B) :
   128	    ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE W W' hle).hom
   129	        ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B W r) =
   130	      (relCurve C B').overAlgebraMap B' W' (algebraMap B B' r) := by
   131	  have hmor : ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
   132	        (snd C (overSpec k B)).left.appLE ⊤ W
   133	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge)) ≫
   134	      (relCurveMap C B B').appLE W W' hle =
   135	      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B') ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv ≫
   136	        (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
   137	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge) := by
   138	    have hnat : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
   139	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appTop =
   140	        CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B') ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv := by
   141	      rw [Iso.inv_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc,
   142	        ← Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B')),
   143	        Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
   144	    have hsplit : ((snd C (overSpec k B')).left ≫
   145	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ W'
   146	          ((relCurveMap_snd C B B') ▸
   147	            hle.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono _ (le_top.trans
   148	              (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge))) =
   149	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ ⊤
   150	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top _).ge ≫
   151	          (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
   152	            (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge) :=
   153	      (Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE _ _ _ _ _ _ _).symm
   154	    have happ : (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ ⊤
   155	        (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top _).ge =
   156	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appTop :=
   157	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
   158	    rw [Category.assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE,
   159	      appLE_congr_hom (relCurveMap_snd C B B'), hsplit, happ, ← Category.assoc,
   160	      hnat, Category.assoc]
   161	  have hoam : (relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B W r =
   162	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
   163	        (snd C (overSpec k B)).left.appLE ⊤ W
   164	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge)).hom
   165	        r := rfl
   166	  have hoam' : (relCurve C B').overAlgebraMap B' W' (algebraMap B B' r) =
   167	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv ≫
   168	        (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
   169	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge)).hom
   170	        (algebraMap B B' r) := rfl
   171	  rw [hoam, hoam']
   172	  exact congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $hmor) r)

/-- **Stacks 02KG (`i = 0`), affine morphisms, arbitrary base change**: for a
cartesian square of schemes

```
  X' --g'--> X
  |f'        |f
  v          v
  Y' --g---> Y
```

with `f` and `f'` affine and `F` quasi-coherent on `X`, the canonical
base-change comparison `g^*(f_* F) ⟶ f'_*((g')^* F)` is an isomorphism — with
**no flatness hypothesis on `g`**.  Checked on the basis of affine opens of
`Y'` contained in the `g`-preimage of an affine open of `Y`
(`Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_isBasis` +
`isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_app_of_isPullback`). -/
theorem isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g' : X' ⟶ X}
    (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsAffineHom f] [IsAffineHom f']

    IsIso (pushforwardBaseChangeMap f g f' g' h.w F) := by
  refine Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_isBasis
    (ι := {p : Y'.Opens × Y.Opens //
      IsAffineOpen p.1 ∧ IsAffineOpen p.2 ∧ p.1 ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ p.2})
    (B := fun p => p.1.1) ?_ _ ?_
  · rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd]
    intro W y hy
    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hgyV, -⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
      (Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens Y)
      (show g.base y ∈ (⊤ : Y.Opens) from trivial)
    have hyWV : y ∈ W ⊓ g ⁻¹ᵁ V := ⟨hy, hgyV⟩
    obtain ⟨O, hOaff, hyO, hOsub⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
      (Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens Y') hyWV
    exact ⟨O, ⟨⟨(O, V), hOaff, hVaff, hOsub.trans inf_le_right⟩, rfl⟩, hyO,
      hOsub.trans inf_le_left⟩
  · intro p
    exact isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_app_of_isPullback h F p.2.2.2 p.2.2.1 p.2.1

/-- **The 02KG base-change isomorphism** for an affine morphism, bundled form:
`g^*(f_* F) ≅ f'_*((g')^* F)` for a cartesian square with `f`, `f'` affine and
`F` quasi-coherent — no flatness on `g`. -/
noncomputable def pushforwardPullbackBaseChangeIso
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g' : X' ⟶ X}
    (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsAffineHom f] [IsAffineHom f']
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) :=
  haveI := isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback h F
  asIso (pushforwardBaseChangeMap f g f' g' h.w F)

end AffineBaseChangeIso

/-! ## §7. The fibre-compatibility isomorphism and the `hH1`/`hH0` transfers

Specializing the 02KG isomorphism to the fibre square of
`π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` over a scheme point `t : Spec A`
(`isPullback_finiteMapToP1FiberMap`) produces the fibre-compatibility
isomorphism of transfer item (c),

`(p.fiberι t)^* ((π_A)_* L) ≅ (π_t)_* ((q.fiberι t)^* L)`,

for **every** scheme point `t` — `κ(t)` is not flat over `A`, which is exactly
why the arbitrary-pushout form of 02KG (and never the flat 02KE engine) is used.
From it:

* `hH0` is discharged **verbatim**
  (`pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH0`): the isomorphism restricts
  to a `κ(t)`-linear equivalence on global sections over the fibre, because
  `π_t` is a `κ(t)`-morphism (`finiteMapToP1FiberMap_toSpecResidueField`);
/-- **B3 headline, local-freeness half** (extraction from the gate): for an
invertible `L` on `C_A` with fibrewise `h¹ = 0` at all scheme points, the
pushforward `q_* L` is, near every `t : Spec A`, free of rank
`h⁰(C_t, L_t) = χ(L_t)`. -/
theorem pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing [HasRigidPushforward C]
    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
    (h1 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t)
    (t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :
    ∃ U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens, t ∈ U ∧

            (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L) ≅
        _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)

            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t)))) :=

same hypotheses, the formation of `q_* L` commutes with every ring map
`A → A'`. -/

    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
    (h1 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),

section RankOneCorollary

/-- **Rank-one local freeness gives local triviality** (scaffold brick for the

(`coproductUniqueIso`, as in `LineBundle.freeUnitIso`). -/
theorem LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M ≅

have hres : ∀ (W₀ : X.Opens) (hW₀ : W₀ ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : Y.Opens))
      (hW'' : g' ⁻¹ᵁ W₀ ≤ f' ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : Y'.Opens)),

          (pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap g' M e' x)
        = pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap g' M (le_refl (g' ⁻¹ᵁ W₀))

      (le_refl (g' ⁻¹ᵁ W₀)) hW₀ hW'' x

        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M), (⊤ : Y'.Opens)) from
      pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap g' M e' x))) = Ξ (b ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, ⊤)] (E (T x))) := by
    rw [_root_.map_smul T' b, _root_.map_smul E' b]
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    rw [hΞ b (E (T x))]
    exact Prod.ext
      (congrArg (fun z => (f'.appLE (⊤ : Y'.Opens) (g' ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.U₁) le_top).hom b • z)
        (hres 𝒰.U₁ le_top le_top))
      (congrArg (fun z => (f'.appLE (⊤ : Y'.Opens) (g' ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.U₂) le_top).hom b • z)
        (hres 𝒰.U₂ le_top le_top))

/-! ## §2. The gate's remaining statement, for an AJC curve -/

section AJC

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- Elaborating the engine application unfolds two nested pullback squares and the full
-- `letI` dictionary of the preimage cover.
/-- **`RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange` is a theorem.**  For the AJC curve `C/k` and every
finitely generated `k`-algebra `A`, the formation of `Γ(C_A, L)` for an invertible `L` with
fibrewise `h¹ = 0` commutes with every ring map `A → A'`.

The Čech `H⁰`-purity fed to §1 is obtained on the 2-affine cover
`(p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage π_A` of `C_A` — the preimage under the finite (hence
affine) `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` of the standard 2-chart cover of `ℙ¹_A` — from two inputs:

* **surjectivity** of its Čech differential, which is the *first* conjunct of the ℙ¹ engine
  `p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing_of_isIntegral` applied to `(π_A)_* L`.  No
  transport is needed: `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_pushforward` is `rfl` and
  `moduleSectionDiffBase`'s underlying function *is* `moduleSectionDiff`, so the two
  surjectivity statements are the same proposition — in particular the propositional
  `q = π_A ≫ p` never has to be crossed;
* **flatness** of `Γ(L, U₁ ⊓ U₂)` over `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`, which is `CoherentSheafFlat q L` read at
  the pair `(⊤, U₁ ⊓ U₂)` (`flat_baseSections_of_coherentSheafFlat`) — stated for `q` from the
  start, so again no transport.

`bijective_kerBaseChange_of_surjective` then gives purity at `q`'s own module structures.  (The
alternative recorded in `Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean` — instantiating the engine's
*fourth* conjunct instead — avoids the flatness obligation but has to move the whole `letI`
dictionary from `p` and the pushforward module to `q` and `L`; flatness is free here, so this
route is shorter.)

The ℙ¹ engine's `H⁰`-finiteness anchor is `IsIntegral (ℙ¹_k)`
(`Adelic.instIsIntegralP1OverLeft`), so the two fields of the gate are not independent — as
`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean`'s dependency warning records. -/
theorem rigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange_proved
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] :
    RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange C A := by
  intro L hL h1 A' _ φ e'
  haveI := hL.isFinitePresentation
  haveI : IsFinite (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C) := isFinite_finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C
  haveI := pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_isFinitePresentation A C L hL
  -- the ℙ¹ engine, applied to the finite pushforward `(π_A)_* L`
  have hengine := p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing_of_isIntegral A
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L)
    (pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_coherentSheafFlat A C L hL)
    (p1CechFibrewiseBridge_proved A
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L) inferInstance
      (fun t => pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH1 A C L t hL (h1 t)))
  -- the module dictionary on `C_A` for the preimage cover
  letI c1 := (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule
    L ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₁
  letI c2 := (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule
    L ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₂
  letI c0 := (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule
    L (((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₁ ⊓
      ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₂)
  -- surjectivity of the Čech differential of the preimage cover: the same proposition
  have hd : Function.Surjective
      ⇑(((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage
          (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).moduleSectionDiffBase
        (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) L) :=
    hengine.1
  -- flatness of the overlap sections, read off `CoherentSheafFlat q L`
  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
  haveI : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat C.hom := inferInstance
  haveI : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat
      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) := inferInstance
  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
      Γ(L, ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₁ ⊓
        ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).U₂) :=
    Scheme.flat_baseSections_of_coherentSheafFlat _ L
      (Scheme.coherentSheafFlat_of_isLocallyTrivial_of_flat _ hL)
      ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).isAffineOpen_inf
with fibrewise `h¹ = 0`, and every ring map `φ : A → A'`, the canonical additive map
`Γ(Spec A', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(C_A, L) → Γ(C_{A'}, (g')^* L)`,
`b ⊗ x ↦ b · (base-map image of x)`, is bijective.  This is the module-level residue of
`Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` after affine-target descent.

The existential over `s` is not a loophole: `s` is additive and its values are prescribed on
simple tensors, which generate the tensor product as an abelian group, so `s` is determined
uniquely and the statement really asserts bijectivity of the canonical map. -/
def RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules),
    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
    (∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t) →
    ∀ (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] (φ : A →+* A')
      (e' : (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A')).Opens) ≤
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) ⁻¹ᵁ
          ((pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) ⁻¹ᵁ
            (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens))),
      letI : Algebra Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A'), ⊤) :=
        ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)).appLE
          (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens)
          (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A')).Opens) le_top).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ s : TensorProduct Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A'), ⊤)
          Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd C.hom
              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L,
            (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens)) →+
        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj L),
          (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A')).Opens)),
        (∀ b x, s (b ⊗ₜ[Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)] x) =
          b • (show Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom
                  (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
                  (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj
                ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom
                  (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
                  (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj L),
                (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A')).Opens)) from
            pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap
              (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) L e' x)) ∧
        Function.Bijective s

-- Unfolding `RigidPushforwardBaseChange` exposes two nested pullback squares of schemes.
set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- The `Γ`-level data supplied by `hgamma` is stated for the tautological square and must be
-- matched with the mate's arguments below reducible transparency.
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **The gate's `baseChange` field from the `Γ`-level leaf.**  For a proper `C`, the second
field of `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` follows from the single `Γ`-level bijectivity
`RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange C A`, by affine-target descent (§1–§3). -/
theorem rigidPushforwardBaseChange_of_gamma
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (hgamma : RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange C A) :
    Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange C A := by
  intro L hL h1 A' _ φ
  haveI : IsProper (pullback.snd C.hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) :=
    MorphismProperty.pullback_snd (P := @IsProper) _ _ inferInstance
  haveI : IsProper (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) :=
    MorphismProperty.pullback_snd (P := @IsProper) _ _ inferInstance
  haveI := hL.isFinitePresentation
  haveI : L.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
  haveI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd C.hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L).IsQuasicoherent :=
    Scheme.Modules.pushforward_isQuasicoherent _ L
  have e' : (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A')).Opens) ≤
      (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) ⁻¹ᵁ
        ((pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) ⁻¹ᵁ
          (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens)) := by simp
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hbij⟩ := hgamma L hL h1 A' φ e'
  exact isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_bijective_gamma _ _ _ _ pullback.condition L e' s hs hbij
